transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-11 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Kim (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CS), Dr. Sara Lim (CISO, Avalon), Tom Reeves (VP Eng), Anita Gomez (Legal), Luis Martinez (Cloud Eng)

Summary (auto):
Redwood ran through high-level controls and deployment options. Avalon emphasized compliance needs (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001), ability to use customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), SAML SSO + SCIM user provisioning, RBAC granularity, immutable audit logs with at least 13 months retention, and explicit deletion guarantees for data. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC peering) vs Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem). Next steps and owners agreed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Sara (Avalon): hi, sara lim here, chief information security officer at avalon, i'll lead the compliance side.
[00:13] Tom (Avalon): tom reaves, vp engineering, i own infra and cost questions.
[00:17] Anita (Avalon): anita gomez, legal, i will review DPA and residency stuff.
[00:21] Maya: great, ethan from our SE team will go over the technical controls and i will handle process and timelines.
[00:26] Ethan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks. just to set expectations, this call is discovery of security posture — we'll clarify what evidence you need and what deployment mode fits best.

[02:05] Ethan: quickly, on certifications, redwood has SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 — we can share the attestation and certs. how recent do you need them?
[02:14] Dr. Sara: SOC2 type two within last 12 months is mandatory, and ISO preferred. we also usually ask for the auditor name and scope.
[02:23] Maya: yes we can provide a copy of the SOC2 (CrowneSec audit firm) and ISO27001 scope doc; i'll attach those.

[04:10] Tom: on deployments — can you explain the difference between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private again? we want to understand where customer data lives and network boundaries.
[04:21] Ethan: sure — Hosted is our shared tenant, fully managed, low friction. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools logically isolated for you with VPC peering and dedicated capacity, we provide SLA-backed throughput. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane option — either VPC-hosted private control plane or on-prem packaged deployment for air-gapped environments.
[04:45] Tom: when you say VPC peering for Dedicated, is traffic ever routed through third-party storages? we need to avoid unwanted egress.
[04:54] Ethan: data for inference stays in-region; logs and metrics can be pushed to your S3 if you choose, otherwise they remain in our audited storage. we can also set up private link / VPC endpoints to avoid public internet egress.

[07:00] Dr. Sara: BYOK is a hard requirement for some of our workloads. do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[07:10] Maya: yes we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have managed KMS by default but BYOK is available for enterprise tiers. we integrate with major KMS providers and offer HSM-backed key wrapping for encryption at rest.
[07:26] Ethan: technically we use AES-256 for data at rest; keys are wrapped with customer keys when BYOK is enabled. we also support KMIP-compatible HSMs for on-prem.

[09:40] Anita: legal will want specific contract language around key custody and deletion. if a key is revoked do you guarantee immediate deletion of ciphertext and backups?
[09:52] Maya: we can add clauses for key revocation and data access. deletion guarantees — we can provide documented workflows: logical deletion, followed by secure shredding of backups per SLA. we'll need to align retention windows.

[12:12] Tom: audit logs — we need immutable logs retained for at least 13 months and exportable to our SIEM. how do you handle audit logs and access trail?
[12:24] Ethan: we provide tamper-evident audit logs with append-only storage. you can stream logs to your S3 or to our log export endpoint; retention by default is 90 days in hosted analytics but for enterprise we can extend to 13+ months and support WORM-like storage for immutability.
[12:48] Dr. Sara: do logs include token-level data? we need PII redaction and token-level cost traces but not raw PII.
[13:00] Ethan: logs are configurable; we redact sensitive fields by default and provide anonymized token-level metrics. for debugging we can provide limited salted traces under NDAs.

[15:30] Luis (Avalon): on SSO, we use Okta and expect SAML + SCIM provisioning. are you supporting SCIM for groups and role mapping?
[15:40] Ethan: yes SAML SSO is supported, SCIM for provisioning is supported and we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles. we have a sample assertion mapping in our docs.
[16:02] Maya: we'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints after the call.

[18:10] Tom: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles, separation of duties, and audit of admin actions. can you enforce least privilege?
[18:20] Ethan: our RBAC model includes: admin/org-owner, infra-admin, app-deployer, auditor, read-only roles. you can create custom roles too. admin actions are logged in the audit trail and we support MFA on admin accounts.

[21:05] Dr. Sara: data residency — some PHI workflows must remain in Canada. can you guarantee regional residency?
[21:14] Maya: yes, regional hosting is available; Dedicated and Private let you pin region and control data egress. for Hosted we have region options and contractual commitments for data residency.

[24:00] Anita: retention and deletion policy — we typically require 7 year records for certain audits, but for LLM logs we want at least 13 months; also a policy for prompt retention (30/90 days) depending on sensitivity.
[24:18] Ethan: prompts and inputs are configurable — default ephemeral cache is 30 days; hosted uses 90 days by default for analytics. we can set retention per-route and support auto-deletion on demand for PII.

[27:05] Tom: performance tradeoffs — if we enable BYOK and extra logging what is the p50 latency hit?
[27:14] Ethan: minimal; BYOK adds key unwrap step (milliseconds). detailed numbers depend on model and sequence length but we can run a bench on Dedicated to compare. caching (KV cache) and batching help keep latency down.

[30:30] Dr. Sara: incident response — what is your process and RTO for security incidents?
[30:40] Maya: we have an IR playbook, SOC on-call, and will notify customers per SLA. we offer optional 24/7 incident support in enterprise packages.

[33:00] Anita: legal — any sub-processors? we need list and subprocessors agreement.
[33:10] Maya: yes we'll send current sub-processor list and update process.

[35:40] Tom: do you have customer references for similar regulated customers? healthcare or finance?
[35:49] Maya: yes, i'll share anonymized references (several healthcare customers use Dedicated/Private).

[37:30] Ethan: technical note — for Private on-prem deployment we provide an installable package that runs inference in your network. control plane can be customer-managed; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM with no data leaving your VPC.

[40:05] Luis: networking — will we need to open egress ports for model downloads/updates?
[40:12] Ethan: model downloads can be staged via your internal repo or via signed allowed endpoints; for air-gapped setups we support offline model images.

[42:30] Maya: recap — action items: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, SAML/SCIM guide, RBAC doc, VPC peering diagram and draft DPA redline. you (Anita) will send the legal checklist and Luis will share infra diagram.
[42:45] Anita: thanks, we'll review and get back with any contract redlines.
[43:00] Tom: aim is to decide on pilot by end of year and run a technical deep dive next week.
[43:10] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the security pack. thanks everyone.
[46:00] Meeting end
